title: Signing off on your own screen
eyebrow: Watched on your own board: two jobs waiting on you, nothing to press

actions.fyi: Nothing is waiting on you. Override any decision below if you disagree with one.

content.label: What you found
content.lead: The button that finishes a job is drawn on the agents' column and never on yours.

rows: Who the column is waiting on
What a session is allowed to do
refused, on the grounds you sign it on your screen

blocks.text: So the one column that can only be finished by you is the one column with no way to finish anything. The only route left was the state menu buried inside a card's own panel.

Counted on your board this morning, column by column: two jobs standing in Manager Review, and zero buttons that finish one — the first of them is 12 of 12 finished, every piece closed, waiting only on you.

content.label: What it is now
content.lead: The button sits on your column and the agents' one is bare.

rows: A job still waiting on a reading
offers a finish you should not give

before.caption: Before — 12 of 12 finished, waiting on you, nothing to press

after.caption: After — the same card, with your sign-off on it

blocks.text: Held in place two ways: four checks on the card itself, and one that opens the board in a real browser and reads the buttons off each column. Built with the button back on the agents' column, both go red at once — so it cannot drift back unnoticed, and it cannot drift back between the code and what you are served.

decisions.title: The button moves rather than appearing in both columns
decisions.why: A job in the agents' column has not been read yet. Leaving a finish button there is what let work reach done without anyone signing it, which is the complaint that opened the six columns in the first place.

decisions.title: No send-back button in this change
decisions.why: Turning a job down is a conversation, not a press: the machinery already tells a session to say what is wrong and leave the card where it is. Adding a second button before that is settled would guess at what turning down means.

next.if_nothing: The fix lands on its own and your column gains the button; nothing else changes.

steps.step: Your column gains the button that finishes a job, and the agents' column loses it
A check that goes red if the button ever drifts back to the wrong column
